title: Louvres rotated by length
summary: A row of blades of increasing length is rotated so each blade's angle follows its own length: short blades stay flat, long blades turn - the logic behind graded shading louvres.
how_to_use: 'Blade count' sets the number of blades; 'Base length', 'Growth step' and 'Growth power' shape how blade lengths grow along the row.
Edit the two small panels to set the angle range in multiples of pi - 0.5 means a quarter turn.
Bake 'Rotate' to get the rotated blades (the unrotated ones are shown in a second colour).
concepts: Bounds + Remap Numbers: mapping one range (lengths) onto another (angles)

steps.title: 1  INPUTS - change these
steps.explain: How many blades, how their length grows, and the angle range (in multiples of pi).

steps.title: 2  Blades of growing length
steps.explain: Series gives each blade a Y position. A second Series plus Base length, raised to Growth power, gives a non-linear length per blade. Construct Point and Line draw each blade from the Y axis out to its length.

steps.title: 3  Length to angle
steps.explain: Bounds finds the shortest and longest blade. Remap Numbers maps every length from that range onto the angle range set in the panels, and Pi turns it into radians.

steps.title: 4  RESULT - rotated louvres
steps.explain: Rotate turns each blade in the XZ plane by its own angle. Two Custom Previews show the original and the rotated blades in different colours.
